title: Rural consumption per person
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 2 — ECONOMY: WHAT A MONTH COSTS
subtitle:
Average monthly spending per person in rural India, HCES 2023-24.
Chhattisgarh ₹2,739. Sikkim ₹9,377. The national figure is ₹4,122.
callout_note: ₹ a month per person in rural {state}, the highest of any state or territory
takeaway: Rural spending per person runs from ₹2,739 in Chhattisgarh to ₹9,377 in Sikkim, a gap of 3.4 times inside one country.
policy: A single national poverty line converted at one price level treats these as the same economy. State-specific price deflators are not a refinement here, they are the difference between a real estimate and an arithmetic one.
takeaway_hi: ग्रामीण भारत में प्रति व्यक्ति मासिक खर्च छत्तीसगढ़ में ₹2,739 से लेकर सिक्किम में ₹9,377 तक है — एक ही देश के भीतर साढ़े तीन गुना का अंतर।
title_hi: ग्रामीण प्रति व्यक्ति उपभोग व्यय

title: Urban consumption per person
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 2 — ECONOMY: WHAT A MONTH COSTS
subtitle:
The same survey, urban areas. Chhattisgarh ₹4,927, Sikkim ₹13,927.
The urban figure exceeds the rural one in every state without exception.
callout_note: ₹ a month per person in urban {state}, against ₹6,996 nationally
takeaway: Urban spending per person is higher than rural spending in all 36 states and territories. The national gap is ₹6,996 against ₹4,122, about 70 per cent.
policy: Urban-rural is the axis most Indian transfer programmes are least able to see: entitlements are settled at the village or ward, while the gap that drives migration sits between them.
takeaway_hi: सभी 36 राज्यों और केंद्रशासित प्रदेशों में शहरी प्रति व्यक्ति खर्च ग्रामीण खर्च से अधिक है। राष्ट्रीय अंतर लगभग 70 प्रतिशत है।
title_hi: शहरी प्रति व्यक्ति उपभोग व्यय

title: Rural consumption inequality
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 2 — ECONOMY: WHO GETS WHAT
callout_note: Gini in rural {state}, the widest rural spread in the country
takeaway: Kerala has the seventh highest rural spending per person of 36 states and territories and the second most unequal rural distribution, at a Gini of 0.255 against 0.237 nationally. A high average is not a flat one.
policy: Ranking states by mean consumption and ranking them by its dispersion produce different lists. Any transfer designed off the mean alone is targeting a state that does not exist.
takeaway_hi: केरल में ग्रामीण खर्च का स्तर भी ऊंचा है और उसका फैलाव भी — गिनी 0.255, राष्ट्रीय 0.237 के मुकाबले।
title_hi: ग्रामीण उपभोग असमानता

title: Urban consumption inequality
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 2 — ECONOMY: WHO GETS WHAT
subtitle:
The same measure in urban areas: 0.284 nationally against 0.237 rural,
and higher than the rural figure in 31 of 36 states and territories.
Jharkhand and Ladakh are the widest, Nagaland and Manipur the narrowest.
callout_note: Gini in urban {state}, the widest urban spread in the country
takeaway: Urban consumption is more unequal than rural consumption in 31 of 36 states and territories. The five exceptions are small island and hill units. Jharkhand has among the lowest urban spending per person and the widest spread.
policy: Cities are where the dispersion is, and where the instruments are weakest: urban India has no counterpart to the rural employment guarantee.
takeaway_hi: लगभग हर राज्य में शहरी उपभोग ग्रामीण उपभोग से अधिक असमान है। झारखंड में शहरी खर्च कम है और फैलाव सबसे अधिक।
title_hi: शहरी उपभोग असमानता

title: Female labour force participation
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 4 — GENDER: WHO IS COUNTED AS WORKING
subtitle:
Women aged 15 and above working or looking for work, PLFS 2025.
Delhi 13.1 per cent. Sikkim 66.7. The national figure is 40.0.
callout_note: of women aged 15 and above are in the labour force in {state}
takeaway: Delhi records the lowest female labour force participation in the country at 13.1 per cent, five times below Sikkim's 66.7. Income and participation do not move together across states.
policy: Participation measured on usual status counts unpaid family labour on a farm and does not count housework. Much of the state-to-state range is a measurement boundary, and reading it as a preference is how the number gets misused.
takeaway_hi: दिल्ली में महिला श्रम बल भागीदारी देश में सबसे कम है, 13.1 प्रतिशत — सिक्किम के 66.7 से पाँच गुना कम।
title_hi: महिला श्रम बल भागीदारी

title: Gender gap in literacy
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 4 — GENDER: WHAT WAS NOT TAUGHT
callout_note: percentage points between male and female literacy in {state}
takeaway: Rajasthan's literacy gap is 23.2 percentage points, ten times Kerala's 2.2. The 14 states left grey are not included in the published round.
policy: A literacy gap among people aged 7 and above is an accumulated record, not a current one: it holds decades of school enrolment inside a single number, and closing it has a floor set by how long people live.
takeaway_hi: राजस्थान में साक्षरता का लैंगिक अंतर 23.2 प्रतिशत बिंदु है, केरल के 2.2 से दस गुना अधिक।
title_hi: साक्षरता में लैंगिक अंतर

title: Child stunting, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: HOW TALL CHILDREN GROW
subtitle:
Children under 5 who are stunted, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Puducherry 16.6 per cent. Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu 37.1. India 29.3, down from 35.5 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of children under 5 are stunted in {state}, the highest of any state or territory with a figure
takeaway: Between 16.6 per cent in Puducherry and 37.1 per cent in Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, stunting still differs by more than two times across the country. The India figure fell from 35.5 to 29.3 per cent between NFHS-5 and NFHS-6.
policy: A national fall hides states that moved the other way. Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep rose, so a programme judged on the India average would miss them.
takeaway_hi: पुडुचेरी में 16.6 प्रतिशत से दादरा और नागर हवेली और दमन और दीव में 37.1 प्रतिशत तक, बौनापन अब भी दो गुना से अधिक अलग है। NFHS-5 से NFHS-6 के बीच भारत का आँकड़ा 35.5 से घटकर 29.3 प्रतिशत हो गया।
title_hi: बाल बौनापन, NFHS-6

title: Institutional births, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: WHERE BIRTHS HAPPEN
subtitle:
Births in a health facility in the five years before the survey, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Nagaland 62.2 per cent. Lakshadweep 100.0. India 90.6, up from 88.6 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of births took place in a health facility in {state}
takeaway: Nearly every birth now happens in a facility in most states, with Lakshadweep at 100.0 per cent. Nagaland, at 62.2 per cent, is the clear outlier, and India stands at 90.6 per cent, up from 88.6.
policy: When the national figure is near 90 per cent, the remaining gap is concentrated in a few states and in the most remote households, and it needs targeted delivery rather than another national drive.
takeaway_hi: अधिकांश राज्यों में लगभग हर प्रसव अब स्वास्थ्य संस्थान में होता है, लक्षद्वीप में 100.0 प्रतिशत। नागालैंड 62.2 प्रतिशत के साथ स्पष्ट अपवाद है, और भारत का आँकड़ा 88.6 से बढ़कर 90.6 प्रतिशत है।
title_hi: संस्थागत प्रसव, NFHS-6

title: Women who have used the internet, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  EDUCATION: WHO IS ONLINE
subtitle:
Women aged 15-49 who have ever used the internet, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Tripura 48.8 per cent. Goa 94.0. India 64.3, nearly double the 33.3 of NFHS-5.
callout_note: of women aged 15-49 have ever used the internet in {state}
takeaway: The share of women who have ever used the internet nearly doubled between the two rounds, from 33.3 to 64.3 per cent. It still runs from 48.8 per cent in Tripura to 94.0 per cent in Goa.
policy: Ever having used the internet is a low bar. It says nothing about owning a phone, reading confidently online, or using a service independently, so it should not be read as digital inclusion.
takeaway_hi: दो दौर के बीच कभी इंटरनेट इस्तेमाल करने वाली महिलाओं का हिस्सा लगभग दोगुना होकर 33.3 से 64.3 प्रतिशत हो गया। फिर भी यह त्रिपुरा में 48.8 प्रतिशत से गोवा में 94.0 प्रतिशत तक है।
title_hi: इंटरनेट इस्तेमाल करने वाली महिलाएँ, NFHS-6

title: Women with a bank account they use, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  GENDER: WHO HOLDS THE ACCOUNT
subtitle:
Women aged 15-49 with a bank or savings account they themselves use, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Meghalaya 81.5 per cent. Ladakh 95.5. India 89.0, up from 78.6 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of women aged 15-49 have a bank or savings account they use themselves in {state}
takeaway: Access to an account women use themselves has become close to universal. The gap between states shrank to 14 points, from 81.5 per cent in Meghalaya to 95.5 per cent in Ladakh.
policy: An account that a woman uses herself is not the same as control over the money in it. Survey figures on decisions and earnings are the next question to ask.
takeaway_hi: महिलाओं द्वारा स्वयं उपयोग किए जाने वाले खाते की पहुँच लगभग सार्वभौमिक हो गई है। राज्यों के बीच अंतर घटकर 14 अंक रह गया, मेघालय में 81.5 प्रतिशत से लद्दाख में 95.5 प्रतिशत तक।
title_hi: स्वयं उपयोग किए जाने वाले बैंक खाते वाली महिलाएँ, NFHS-6

title: Spousal violence, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  GENDER: WHAT WOMEN REPORT
subtitle:
Ever-married women aged 18-49 who have ever experienced spousal violence, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Ladakh 1.9 per cent. Bihar 36.1. India 22.3, down from 29.2 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of ever-married women aged 18-49 report spousal violence in {state}
takeaway: Reported spousal violence runs from 1.9 per cent in Ladakh to 36.1 per cent in Bihar. The India figure is 22.3 per cent, down from 29.2 in NFHS-5.
policy: These are what women told interviewers, and a low figure can mean low violence or low willingness to report it. Some state changes between rounds are very large, so read a single state with care.
takeaway_hi: रिपोर्ट की गई पति द्वारा हिंसा लद्दाख में 1.9 प्रतिशत से बिहार में 36.1 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 22.3 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 29.2 था।
title_hi: पति द्वारा हिंसा, NFHS-6

title: Women married before 18, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  GENDER: HOW EARLY MARRIAGE HAPPENS
subtitle:
Women aged 20-24 who were married before age 18, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Kerala 2.9 per cent. West Bengal 36.4. India 20.1, down from 23.3 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of women aged 20-24 were married before 18 in {state}
takeaway: Child marriage fell nationally from 23.3 to 20.1 per cent, but it is still 36.4 per cent in West Bengal, more than twelve times the 2.9 per cent of Kerala.
policy: Andaman and Nicobar and Tamil Nadu have no published figure in the fact sheets, so they are grey. A grey state here has no figure, not a low one.
takeaway_hi: बाल विवाह राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर 23.3 से घटकर 20.1 प्रतिशत हुआ, पर पश्चिम बंगाल में यह अब भी 36.4 प्रतिशत है, जो केरल के 2.9 प्रतिशत से बारह गुना से अधिक है।
title_hi: 18 से पहले विवाहित महिलाएँ, NFHS-6

title: Child wasting, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: WEIGHT FOR HEIGHT
subtitle:
Share of children under 5 whose weight for height is more than two standard deviations below the WHO standard, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Mizoram 8.1 per cent. Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu 24.2. India 19.0, down from 19.3 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of children under 5 are wasted in {state}, the highest of any state or territory with a figure
takeaway: Children under 5 who are wasted ranges from 8.1 per cent in Mizoram to 24.2 per cent in Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. The India figure is 19.0 per cent, down from 19.3 in NFHS-5.
policy: Wasting reflects recent shortfalls in food and bouts of illness, so it can move faster than stunting. One survey year is not a trend.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 8.1 से 24.2 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 19.0 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 19.3 था।
title_hi: बाल दुबलापन (वेस्टिंग), NFHS-6

title: Underweight children, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: WEIGHT FOR AGE
subtitle:
Share of children under 5 whose weight for age is more than two standard deviations below the WHO standard, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Sikkim 11.2 per cent. Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu 41.3. India 31.8, down from 32.1 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of children under 5 are underweight in {state}, the highest of any state or territory with a figure
takeaway: Children under 5 who are underweight ranges from 11.2 per cent in Sikkim to 41.3 per cent in Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. The India figure is 31.8 per cent, down from 32.1 in NFHS-5.
policy: Underweight mixes stunting and wasting, so it is a rougher guide than either measure alone.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 11.2 से 41.3 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 31.8 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 32.1 था।
title_hi: कम वज़न वाले बच्चे, NFHS-6

title: Exclusive breastfeeding, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: THE FIRST SIX MONTHS
subtitle:
Share of children under 6 months who are exclusively breastfed, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Uttar Pradesh 34.6 per cent. Chhattisgarh 75.8. India 55.8, down from 63.7 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of children under 6 months are exclusively breastfed in {state}, the highest of any state or territory with a figure
takeaway: Exclusive breastfeeding under 6 months ranges from 34.6 per cent in Uttar Pradesh to 75.8 per cent in Chhattisgarh. The India figure is 55.8 per cent, down from 63.7 in NFHS-5.
policy: Mothers report this from recall for their youngest child. Small states rest on few cases, and some have no published figure.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 34.6 से 75.8 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 55.8 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 63.7 था।
title_hi: केवल स्तनपान, NFHS-6

title: Full vaccination, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: THE VACCINATION CARD
subtitle:
Share of children aged 12-23 months fully vaccinated, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Nagaland 64.3 per cent. Goa 93.8. India 82.6, up from 76.6 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of children aged 12-23 months are fully vaccinated in {state}, the highest of any state or territory with a figure
takeaway: Children fully vaccinated, 12-23 months ranges from 64.3 per cent in Nagaland to 93.8 per cent in Goa. The India figure is 82.6 per cent, up from 76.6 in NFHS-5.
policy: The figure combines vaccination cards with the mother's recall, and states with few children in this age group give noisy results.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 64.3 से 93.8 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 82.6 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 76.6 था।
title_hi: पूर्ण टीकाकरण, NFHS-6

title: Caesarean births, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: HOW BIRTHS ARE DELIVERED
subtitle:
Share of births in the five years before the survey delivered by caesarean section, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Meghalaya 6.4 per cent. Telangana 62.2. India 27.2, up from 21.5 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of births were delivered by caesarean section in {state}, the highest of any state or territory with a figure
takeaway: Births delivered by caesarean section ranges from 6.4 per cent in Meghalaya to 62.2 per cent in Telangana. The India figure is 27.2 per cent, up from 21.5 in NFHS-5.
policy: There is no single right rate. Whether a rate reflects need or access is a question this survey cannot answer.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 6.4 से 62.2 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 27.2 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 21.5 था।
title_hi: सिज़ेरियन प्रसव, NFHS-6

title: Women with low BMI, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: ADULT UNDERNUTRITION
subtitle:
Share of women aged 15-49 whose body mass index is below normal, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Andaman and Nicobar 3.1 per cent. Jharkhand 29.2. India 19.7, up from 18.7 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of women aged 15-49 have a BMI below 18.5 in {state}, the highest of any state or territory with a figure
takeaway: Women with bmi below 18.5 ranges from 3.1 per cent in Andaman and Nicobar to 29.2 per cent in Jharkhand. The India figure is 19.7 per cent, up from 18.7 in NFHS-5.
policy: A BMI below 18.5 marks undernutrition in an adult woman, and it moves slowly between survey rounds.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 3.1 से 29.2 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 19.7 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 18.7 था।
title_hi: कम BMI वाली महिलाएँ, NFHS-6

title: Overweight women, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: ADULT OVERWEIGHT
subtitle:
Share of women aged 15-49 with a body mass index of 25.0 or more, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Assam 19.6 per cent. Puducherry 51.3. India 30.7, up from 24.0 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of women aged 15-49 are overweight or obese in {state}, the highest of any state or territory with a figure
takeaway: Women who are overweight or obese ranges from 19.6 per cent in Assam to 51.3 per cent in Puducherry. The India figure is 30.7 per cent, up from 24.0 in NFHS-5.
policy: Overweight now sits beside undernutrition in many states, so one national health message misses both.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 19.6 से 51.3 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 30.7 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 24.0 था।
title_hi: अधिक वज़न वाली महिलाएँ, NFHS-6

title: High blood sugar in women, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: BLOOD SUGAR
subtitle:
Share of women aged 15 and over with blood sugar above 140 mg/dl, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Ladakh 6.7 per cent. Kerala 28.9. India 17.8, up from 13.5 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of women aged 15 and over have high blood sugar or take medicine for it in {state}, the highest of any state or territory with a figure
takeaway: Women with high blood sugar ranges from 6.7 per cent in Ladakh to 28.9 per cent in Kerala. The India figure is 17.8 per cent, up from 13.5 in NFHS-5.
policy: These are random blood sugar readings or reported medication, not a diagnosis of diabetes.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 6.7 से 28.9 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 17.8 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 13.5 था।
title_hi: उच्च रक्त शर्करा वाली महिलाएँ, NFHS-6

title: High blood pressure in women, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: BLOOD PRESSURE
subtitle:
Share of women aged 15 and over with systolic of 140 or more or diastolic of 90 or more, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Uttar Pradesh 12.1 per cent. Sikkim 32.0. India 19.4, down from 21.3 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of women aged 15 and over have elevated blood pressure or take medicine for it in {state}, the highest of any state or territory with a figure
takeaway: Women with elevated blood pressure ranges from 12.1 per cent in Uttar Pradesh to 32.0 per cent in Sikkim. The India figure is 19.4 per cent, down from 21.3 in NFHS-5.
policy: The figure includes people already on medicine, so a high share can reflect disease, screening, or both.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 12.1 से 32.0 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 19.4 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 21.3 था।
title_hi: उच्च रक्तचाप वाली महिलाएँ, NFHS-6

title: High blood pressure in men, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: BLOOD PRESSURE
subtitle:
Share of men aged 15 and over with systolic of 140 or more or diastolic of 90 or more, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Uttar Pradesh 14.1 per cent. Kerala 36.6. India 22.1, down from 24.0 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of men aged 15 and over have elevated blood pressure or take medicine for it in {state}, the highest of any state or territory with a figure
takeaway: Men with elevated blood pressure ranges from 14.1 per cent in Uttar Pradesh to 36.6 per cent in Kerala. The India figure is 22.1 per cent, down from 24.0 in NFHS-5.
policy: The figure includes people already on medicine, so a high share can reflect disease, screening, or both.
takeaway_hi: राज्यों के बीच यह 14.1 से 36.6 प्रतिशत तक है। भारत का आँकड़ा 22.1 प्रतिशत है, जो NFHS-5 में 24.0 था।
title_hi: उच्च रक्तचाप वाले पुरुष, NFHS-6

title: Tobacco use among women, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: TOBACCO

takeaway_hi: मध्य प्रदेश में प्रति लाख अनुसूचित जाति व्यक्तियों पर 68.5 मामले दर्ज हुए, राजस्थान में 57.3 और बिहार में 45.6, जबकि भारत का आँकड़ा 27.7 है। पश्चिम बंगाल में 0.5 (214.6 लाख अनुसूचित जाति आबादी में 116 मामले) और त्रिपुरा में शून्य।
title_hi: अनुसूचित जातियों के विरुद्ध दर्ज अपराध, NCRB 2024

title: Honour killings recorded, NCRB 2024
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  CRIME: HONOUR KILLINGS AS REGISTERED
subtitle:
Murders registered with honour killing as the motive, per crore population, NCRB 2024.
India 0.26: 36 murders in the year.
callout_note: murders per crore people were registered as honour killings in {state}, from a single case
takeaway: NCRB recorded 36 murders with honour killing as the motive in 2024. Bihar had the most (6), then Jharkhand and Punjab (5 each). Manipur has the highest rate, 3.07 per crore, from one case. Twenty-three states and territories recorded none.
policy: A zero means no murder was recorded under this motive, which is not the same as none occurring: a family that reports an honour killing as a suicide or an accident leaves no trace in this table. With counts this small the map is a list of where the motive was written down, and it should not be read as a ranking.
takeaway_hi: NCRB ने 2024 में ऑनर किलिंग को उद्देश्य बताकर 36 हत्याएँ दर्ज कीं। सबसे अधिक बिहार (6) में, फिर झारखंड और पंजाब (5-5) में। मणिपुर की दर सबसे ऊँची (प्रति करोड़ 3.07) है, जो एक ही मामले से बनी है। 23 राज्यों और क्षेत्रों में कोई मामला दर्ज नहीं हुआ।
title_hi: दर्ज ऑनर किलिंग, NCRB 2024

title: Murders linked to witchcraft recorded, NCRB 2024
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  CRIME: WITCH-HUNTING AS REGISTERED
subtitle:
Murders registered with witchcraft as the motive, per crore population, NCRB 2024.
India 0.38: 54 murders in the year.
callout_note: murders per crore people were registered as linked to witchcraft in {state}, from a single case
takeaway: NCRB recorded 54 murders with witchcraft as the motive in 2024. Madhya Pradesh had the most (17), then Chhattisgarh (10) and Odisha (7). Nagaland has the highest rate, 4.42 per crore, from one case, and Chhattisgarh is next at 3.26 from ten. Twenty-five states and territories recorded none.
policy: The table counts murders only. Assaults, banishment and other harm done to people branded as witches are not in it, and a murder is recorded under this motive only if the police write it down. With counts this small, a single case moves a small state to the top.
takeaway_hi: NCRB ने 2024 में डायन/जादू-टोने को उद्देश्य बताकर 54 हत्याएँ दर्ज कीं। सबसे अधिक मध्य प्रदेश (17) में, फिर छत्तीसगढ़ (10) और ओडिशा (7) में। नागालैंड की दर सबसे ऊँची (प्रति करोड़ 4.42) है, जो एक मामले से बनी है; छत्तीसगढ़ 3.26 पर दस मामलों से अगला है। 25 राज्यों और क्षेत्रों में कोई मामला दर्ज नहीं हुआ।
title_hi: डायन-शिकार से जुड़ी दर्ज हत्याएँ, NCRB 2024

title: GSDP per head, MoSPI 2024-25
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 2 · ECONOMY: OUTPUT PER PERSON
subtitle:
Gross state domestic product per head at current prices, Rs, 2024-25.
Sikkim Rs 7.64 lakh, Bihar Rs 0.76 lakh.
callout_note: rupees of output per person in {state}, ten times Bihar's Rs 76,374
takeaway: Sikkim produces Rs 7,63,749 per person and Goa Rs 7,37,738, against Rs 76,374 in Bihar and Rs 1,26,304 in Uttar Pradesh. Eleven of the 32 states and territories with a figure are under Rs 2 lakh per person. Bihar grew 26 per cent in two years at current prices and Goa 36 per cent.
policy: Output per head counts what is produced inside a state, not what its residents earn or keep. Sikkim, Goa, Delhi and Chandigarh are small economies and city-states, so their figures say little about the average household. The 2024-25 figure is an estimate that states revise, and Nagaland and Ladakh have none for the year.
takeaway_hi: सिक्किम में प्रति व्यक्ति 7,63,749 रुपये और गोवा में 7,37,738 रुपये का उत्पादन होता है, जबकि बिहार में 76,374 और उत्तर प्रदेश में 1,26,304। आँकड़े वाले 32 में से 11 राज्यों और क्षेत्रों में यह 2 लाख रुपये से कम है।
title_hi: प्रति व्यक्ति राज्य सकल घरेलू उत्पाद, MoSPI 2024-25

title: Agriculture share of state output, MoSPI 2024-25
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 2 · ECONOMY: HOW STATES EARN
subtitle:
Agriculture, livestock, forestry and fishing as a share of gross state value added,
current prices, 2024-25. Middle state 18.1%.
callout_note: of value added in {state} comes from agriculture, livestock, forestry and fishing
takeaway: Agriculture is 41.3% of Madhya Pradesh's output and 38.0% of Tripura's, against 0.3% in Delhi and 0.5% in Chandigarh. The middle state is at 18.1%. Manipur's share fell most between 2022-23 and 2024-25, by 3.4 points.
policy: A share of output is not a share of jobs, and farm work employs a much larger share of workers than its share of output suggests. The share also falls when other sectors grow faster, so a lower number is not proof that farming did badly.
takeaway_hi: मध्य प्रदेश के उत्पादन में कृषि का हिस्सा 41.3% और त्रिपुरा में 38.0% है, जबकि दिल्ली में 0.3% और चंडीगढ़ में 0.5%। बीच के राज्य में यह 18.1% है।
title_hi: राज्य उत्पादन में कृषि का हिस्सा, MoSPI 2024-25

title: Manufacturing share of state output, MoSPI 2024-25
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 2 · ECONOMY: HOW STATES EARN
subtitle:
Manufacturing as a share of gross state value added, current prices, 2024-25.
Middle state 11.4%.
callout_note: of value added in {state} comes from manufacturing
takeaway: Manufacturing is 38.4% of Sikkim's output, 32.8% of Gujarat's and 27.8% of Goa's, but under 2% in Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Mizoram. The middle state is at 11.4%. Gujarat's share fell 2.1 points in two years and Sikkim's rose 2.7.
policy: In a small economy one large unit can move the share a long way, so Sikkim's figure and the small shares in the north-east and the islands say as much about size as about policy.
takeaway_hi: सिक्किम के उत्पादन में विनिर्माण का हिस्सा 38.4%, गुजरात में 32.8% और गोवा में 27.8% है, जबकि अरुणाचल प्रदेश, मणिपुर और मिज़ोरम में 2% से कम। बीच के राज्य में 11.4%।
title_hi: राज्य उत्पादन में विनिर्माण का हिस्सा, MoSPI 2024-25

title: Services share of state output, MoSPI 2024-25
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  SECTION 2 · ECONOMY: HOW STATES EARN
subtitle:
Services (trade, transport, finance, real estate, public administration and others)
as a share of gross state value added, current prices, 2024-25. Middle state 49.2%.
callout_note: of value added in {state} comes from services
takeaway: Services are 89.4% of Chandigarh's output and 86.1% of Delhi's, and 69.2% of Karnataka's. They are 35.5% in Madhya Pradesh, 32.3% in Chhattisgarh and 29.9% in Sikkim. The middle state is at 49.2%.
policy: Services here include public administration and real estate, which includes the imputed rent of owner-occupied homes, so a high share does not mean a state sells software or finance. Mining, electricity and construction are counted outside services.
takeaway_hi: सेवाएँ चंडीगढ़ के उत्पादन का 89.4%, दिल्ली का 86.1% और कर्नाटक का 69.2% हैं। मध्य प्रदेश में 35.5%, छत्तीसगढ़ में 32.3% और सिक्किम में 29.9%। बीच के राज्य में 49.2%।
title_hi: राज्य उत्पादन में सेवाओं का हिस्सा, MoSPI 2024-25

title: Children with fever or ARI symptoms taken to a health facility, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: CARE FOR SICK CHILDREN
subtitle:
Children under 5 with fever or symptoms of acute respiratory infection in the previous two weeks
who were taken to a health facility or provider, NFHS-6 (2023-24). India 68.8, from 69.0.
callout_note: of sick children were taken for care in {state}, on only 25 to 49 cases. Punjab is next at 86.9
takeaway: Nagaland takes 34.0 per cent of children with fever or breathing symptoms for care, Mizoram 42.2 and Assam 44.4, against 86.9 in Punjab and 80.3 in Karnataka. The India figure is 68.8 per cent, almost unchanged from 69.0 in NFHS-5. Punjab rose 29.6 points and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu fell 14.5.
policy: The figure counts children taken to any health provider, public or private, and says nothing about the quality of care. A figure for a small territory rests on few children, and Chandigarh's 92.1 is based on 25 to 49 cases, so it is flagged and the takeaway compares Punjab, the highest figure without that flag.
takeaway_hi: नागालैंड में बुखार या साँस के लक्षण वाले 34.0 प्रतिशत बच्चों को इलाज के लिए ले जाया गया, मिज़ोरम में 42.2 और असम में 44.4, जबकि पंजाब में 86.9 और कर्नाटक में 80.3। भारत का आँकड़ा 68.8 प्रतिशत है, NFHS-5 के 69.0 से लगभग वही।
title_hi: बुखार या ARI लक्षण वाले बच्चे जिन्हें स्वास्थ्य केंद्र ले जाया गया, NFHS-6

title: Private school enrolment share, UDISE+ 2024-25
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  EDUCATION: WHO RUNS THE SCHOOLS
subtitle:
Share of students in classes 1-12 enrolled in private unaided recognised schools, UDISE+ 2024-25.
India 36.8%, from 31.9% in 2022-23.
callout_note: of students in classes 1-12 attend private unaided schools in {state}
takeaway: Private unaided schools enrol 67.5% of students in Nagaland, 62.7% in Manipur and 60.8% in Telangana, against 7.1% in West Bengal, 12.0% in Goa and 12.7% in Bihar. Across all states and territories the share is 36.8%, up from 31.9% in 2022-23, and it rose in every state and territory.
policy: Government-aided schools are privately managed but publicly funded and are not counted as private here, so a low share can mean a large aided sector rather than a large government one. The two-year rise is large and the source does not say how much of it is a change in the schools or in how they were counted.
title_hi: निजी स्कूलों में नामांकन का हिस्सा, UDISE+ 2024-25

title: Regular employees with no written contract, PLFS 2023-24
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  ECONOMY: THE QUALITY OF SALARIED WORK
subtitle:
Share of regular wage and salaried employees with no written job contract, PLFS 2023-24.
India 58.0%, from 58.6% in 2022-23.
callout_note: of regular wage and salaried employees in {state} have no written job contract
takeaway: In Punjab 84.5% of regular wage and salaried employees have no written contract, in Rajasthan 77.1% and in Gujarat 71.9%, against 10.0% in Arunachal Pradesh, 11.4% in Mizoram and 12.5% in Nagaland. The India figure is 58.0%, from 58.6% a year earlier. Bihar rose 10.1 points in the year.
policy: The measure covers only regular wage and salaried employees, who are a minority of workers. A high share in a state with much private-sector salaried work, and a low one where most salaried jobs are in government, partly reflect who the employers are. A written contract is not the same as social security cover.
takeaway_hi: पंजाब में 84.5% नियमित वेतनभोगी कर्मचारियों के पास लिखित अनुबंध नहीं है, राजस्थान में 77.1% और गुजरात में 71.9%, जबकि अरुणाचल प्रदेश में 10.0%, मिज़ोरम में 11.4% और नागालैंड में 12.5%। भारत का आँकड़ा 58.0% है, जो एक साल पहले 58.6% था।
title_hi: बिना लिखित अनुबंध वाले नियमित कर्मचारी, PLFS 2023-24

title: Men who are overweight or obese, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: BODY WEIGHT
subtitle:
Share of men with a body mass index of 25.0 or more, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
Chandigarh 48.5%, Chhattisgarh 16.1%. India 27.3%, from 22.9% in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of men are overweight or obese in {state}
takeaway: Overweight or obesity affects 48.5 per cent of men in Chandigarh, 46.1 in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and 45.9 in Puducherry, against 16.1 in Chhattisgarh, 17.6 in Madhya Pradesh and 19.3 in Rajasthan. The India figure is 27.3 per cent, up from 22.9 in NFHS-5. Chandigarh rose 14.1 points and Ladakh fell 10.0.
policy: Body mass index counts weight for height and says nothing about diet or fitness. NFHS-6 is provisional, and 27 states and territories carry a figure here.
takeaway_hi: अधिक वज़न या मोटापा चंडीगढ़ में 48.5 प्रतिशत, अंडमान-निकोबार में 46.1 और पुदुचेरी में 45.9 प्रतिशत पुरुषों में है, जबकि छत्तीसगढ़ में 16.1, मध्य प्रदेश में 17.6 और राजस्थान में 19.3। भारत का आँकड़ा 27.3 प्रतिशत है, NFHS-5 के 22.9 से अधिक।
title_hi: अधिक वज़न या मोटापे वाले पुरुष, NFHS-6

title: Installed renewable capacity per person, July 2026
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  ENVIRONMENT: POWER FROM RENEWABLE SOURCES
subtitle:
Installed renewable capacity (solar, wind, hydro including large hydro, bio) in watts per person,
July 2026, on 2024 projected populations. India 208 W.
callout_note: watts of installed renewable capacity per person in {state}
takeaway: Sikkim has 3,350 watts of installed renewable capacity per person, Himachal Pradesh 1,726 and Arunachal Pradesh 1,438, against 208 for India and 5 in Bihar. Gujarat has 724 and Rajasthan 612. Jharkhand and Tripura have 14 each.
policy: This is capacity, not electricity generated: solar and wind plants run for a fraction of the year, and large hydro depends on rain. Large hydro is in MoSPI's total (Himachal Pradesh's 12,980 MW is 11,571 MW of large hydro), and small populations push the per-person figure up. Capacity is for July 2026 and population is a 2024 projection.
takeaway_hi: सिक्किम में प्रति व्यक्ति 3,350 वाट स्थापित नवीकरणीय क्षमता है, हिमाचल प्रदेश में 1,726 और अरुणाचल प्रदेश में 1,438, जबकि भारत का आँकड़ा 208 और बिहार का 5 है। गुजरात में 724 और राजस्थान में 612 है। झारखंड और त्रिपुरा में 14-14।
title_hi: प्रति व्यक्ति स्थापित नवीकरणीय क्षमता, जुलाई 2026

title: Women workers outside agriculture, PLFS 2025
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  ECONOMY: WHERE WOMEN WORK
subtitle:
Share of women workers whose work is outside agriculture, forestry and fishing,
PLFS calendar year 2025. India 40.2%.
callout_note: of women workers in {state} work outside agriculture, forestry and fishing
takeaway: In Chandigarh 99.5% of women workers are outside agriculture and in Delhi 99.3%, against 21.9% in Rajasthan, 22.7% in Himachal Pradesh and 24.4% in Jharkhand. For India the figure is 40.2%: 59.8% of women workers are in agriculture, forestry or fishing.
policy: Counting a woman as a worker includes unpaid work on the family farm, so a low share outside agriculture often means work that carries no wage rather than no work. PLFS was redesigned for 2025, so these figures are not a strict continuation of earlier rounds.
takeaway_hi: चंडीगढ़ में 99.5% और दिल्ली में 99.3% महिला श्रमिक कृषि से बाहर हैं, जबकि राजस्थान में 21.9%, हिमाचल प्रदेश में 22.7% और झारखंड में 24.4%। भारत में यह 40.2% है: 59.8% महिला श्रमिक कृषि, वानिकी या मत्स्य पालन में हैं।
title_hi: कृषि के बाहर काम करने वाली महिला श्रमिक, PLFS 2025

title: Human trafficking cases recorded, NCRB 2024
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  CRIME: HUMAN TRAFFICKING AS REGISTERED
subtitle:
Human trafficking cases registered by the police, per 10 lakh population, NCRB 2024.
India 1.52 (2,135 cases), from 1.55 in 2023.
callout_note: cases per 10 lakh people were registered in {state}, the highest figure (62 cases, up from 18 in 2023)
takeaway: Tripura registered 14.80 human trafficking cases per 10 lakh people (62 cases, up from 18 in 2023) and Telangana 11.04 (423 cases, the most of any state), against 1.52 for India. Arunachal Pradesh is at 5.06 from 8 cases. Seven states and territories registered none, and Assam, West Bengal and Jharkhand, named on the older map, are below 3.
policy: These are registrations by police anti-trafficking units, so a high figure can mean more units actively filing cases rather than more trafficking, and a zero is not proof of none. Fifteen states and territories have fewer than 10 cases, where one case moves the rate a long way. The older map covered 2022, and its ranking has changed.
takeaway_hi: त्रिपुरा में प्रति 10 लाख आबादी पर 14.80 मानव तस्करी के मामले दर्ज हुए (62 मामले, 2023 में 18) और तेलंगाना में 11.04 (423 मामले, किसी भी राज्य में सबसे अधिक), जबकि भारत का आँकड़ा 1.52 है। अरुणाचल प्रदेश 8 मामलों से 5.06 पर है। सात राज्यों और क्षेत्रों में कोई मामला दर्ज नहीं हुआ।
title_hi: दर्ज मानव तस्करी के मामले, NCRB 2024

title: Adult HIV prevalence, NACO 2024
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: HIV
subtitle:
Estimated HIV prevalence among adults, per cent, NACO estimates for 2024.
Mizoram 2.75, Kerala 0.07. India 0.20.
callout_note: per cent of adults are estimated to be living with HIV in {state}
takeaway: Mizoram has the highest estimated adult HIV prevalence at 2.75 per cent, followed by Nagaland at 1.37 and Manipur at 0.81, against 0.20 for India. Jammu and Kashmir has the lowest at 0.06, then Kerala and Jharkhand at 0.07. Andhra Pradesh (0.58) and Karnataka (0.44) are the highest among the large southern states.
policy: These are modelled estimates from surveillance and programme data, not a count of people tested, so small differences between low-prevalence states are within the margin of error. Prevalence is a share of adults. The states with the most people living with HIV in absolute terms differ from those with the highest prevalence.
takeaway_hi: अनुमानित वयस्क एचआईवी प्रसार मिज़ोरम में सबसे अधिक 2.75 प्रतिशत है, फिर नागालैंड में 1.37 और मणिपुर में 0.81, जबकि भारत का आँकड़ा 0.20 है। जम्मू और कश्मीर में सबसे कम 0.06 है, फिर केरल और झारखंड में 0.07।
title_hi: वयस्कों में एचआईवी का प्रसार, NACO 2024

title: Government health spending per person, NHA 2022-23
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: WHO PAYS FOR CARE
subtitle:
Health spending by all government agencies in the state, rupees per person, 2022-23.
21 states covered. Himachal Pradesh Rs 5,913, Bihar Rs 1,056.
callout_note: rupees of government health spending per person in {state}, 5.6 times Bihar's Rs 1,056
takeaway: Government agencies spend Rs 5,913 per person on health in Himachal Pradesh, Rs 3,916 in Jammu and Kashmir and Rs 3,592 in Kerala, against Rs 1,056 in Bihar, Rs 1,419 in Uttar Pradesh and Rs 1,536 in Jharkhand. Only 21 states are covered.
policy: The figure counts spending by the Union, state and local governments inside the state, so it includes central schemes and is not what the state government alone spends. Three of the four highest are hill states (Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Uttarakhand). The 21 states are those for which the estimate can be made; small states, union territories and most of the north-east are not covered.
takeaway_hi: हिमाचल प्रदेश में सरकारी एजेंसियाँ प्रति व्यक्ति 5,913 रुपये स्वास्थ्य पर खर्च करती हैं, जम्मू और कश्मीर में 3,916 और केरल में 3,592, जबकि बिहार में 1,056, उत्तर प्रदेश में 1,419 और झारखंड में 1,536। केवल 21 राज्य शामिल हैं।
title_hi: प्रति व्यक्ति सरकारी स्वास्थ्य व्यय, NHA 2022-23

title: Out-of-pocket share of health spending, NHA 2022-23
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: WHO PAYS FOR CARE
subtitle:
Households' own payments at the point of care, per cent of all health spending in the state,
2022-23. 21 states covered.
callout_note: of all health spending in {state} is paid by households out of pocket
takeaway: Households pay 66.1 per cent of health spending out of pocket in Uttar Pradesh, 64.0 in Kerala, 62.3 in West Bengal and 60.6 in Punjab, against 28.8 in Uttarakhand, 29.2 in Karnataka and 29.7 in Jammu and Kashmir. Bihar is at 47.7. Only 21 states are covered.
policy: A high share is not the same as low public spending: Kerala's total health spending is Rs 13,116 per person and its out-of-pocket spending Rs 8,388 per person. The household figures rest on the NSS 75th round of 2017-18, so state changes since then are not captured.
takeaway_hi: उत्तर प्रदेश में स्वास्थ्य व्यय का 66.1 प्रतिशत परिवार जेब से भरते हैं, केरल में 64.0, पश्चिम बंगाल में 62.3 और पंजाब में 60.6, जबकि उत्तराखंड में 28.8, कर्नाटक में 29.2 और जम्मू और कश्मीर में 29.7। बिहार में 47.7। केवल 21 राज्य शामिल हैं।
title_hi: स्वास्थ्य व्यय में जेब से भुगतान का हिस्सा, NHA 2022-23

title: Public hospital beds per lakh people, March 2023
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: CAPACITY OF THE PUBLIC SYSTEM
subtitle:
Beds in government health centres, sub-district and district hospitals and medical colleges,
per lakh people, 31 March 2023. Maharashtra not shown.
callout_note: public hospital beds per lakh people in {state}
takeaway: Among states, Himachal Pradesh has 136 public hospital beds per lakh people, Kerala 119 and Tamil Nadu 106, against 22 in Bihar, 29 in Jharkhand and 32 in Uttar Pradesh. Lakshadweep (357), the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (340) and Chandigarh (309) are highest of all. Maharashtra is left off.
policy: Maharashtra is grey because the source's medical-college column adds to 16,998 beds more than its printed total, exactly Maharashtra's entry, and the source does not say which is wrong. The count is public beds only, so it says nothing about private hospitals. Beds are for March 2023 and populations are 2024 projections.

title_hi: प्रति लाख आबादी पर सरकारी अस्पताल के बिस्तर, मार्च 2023

title: PM-JAY hospital admissions per lakh people, 2024-25
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: USE OF THE INSURANCE SCHEME
subtitle:
Hospital admissions authorised under PM-JAY in 2024-25, per lakh people.
Delhi, Odisha and West Bengal are not shown.
callout_note: admissions per lakh people were authorised in {state} in 2024-25
takeaway: Meghalaya had 6,785 PM-JAY admissions authorised per lakh people in 2024-25, Chhattisgarh 5,689 and Karnataka 5,574, against 732 in Bihar, 1,043 in Uttar Pradesh and 1,021 in Maharashtra. Kerala fell from 3,397 in 2022-23 to 2,530 and Tamil Nadu from 2,288 to 1,468, while Karnataka rose by 2,474.
policy: The base here is the whole population, not the families covered, so a state that covers more of its people shows a higher figure for that reason alone. Delhi and Odisha joined the scheme in April 2025 and West Bengal is not in it, so they have no figure. Some states run their own schemes beside PM-JAY, which these counts leave out.
takeaway_hi: 2024-25 में मेघालय में प्रति लाख आबादी 6,785 PM-JAY भर्ती स्वीकृत हुईं, छत्तीसगढ़ में 5,689 और कर्नाटक में 5,574, जबकि बिहार में 732, उत्तर प्रदेश में 1,043 और महाराष्ट्र में 1,021। केरल 3,397 से 2,530 पर और तमिलनाडु 2,288 से 1,468 पर आ गया।
title_hi: प्रति लाख आबादी पर PM-JAY अस्पताल भर्ती, 2024-25

title: Mudra loans to SC and ST entrepreneurs, 2022-25
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  CASTE: ACCESS TO CREDIT
subtitle:
PM Mudra Yojana loans to SC and ST entrepreneurs, April 2022 to March 2025,
per lakh SC and ST people. India 12,558.
callout_note: loans to SC and ST entrepreneurs per lakh SC and ST people in {state}, over three years
takeaway: Bihar had 27,973 Mudra loans to SC and ST entrepreneurs per lakh SC and ST people over three years, Haryana 23,274 and Tripura 21,071, against 12,558 for India, and fewer than 1,500 in Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. Uttar Pradesh is at 13,890 and West Bengal at 10,151.
policy: The count is loans, not borrowers, so one entrepreneur with several small loans counts several times. SC and ST are reported together and the population base is the 2011 Census. Loan numbers are those uploaded by lending institutions to the Mudra portal. States with under 1 lakh SC and ST people are left grey.
takeaway_hi: तीन वर्षों में बिहार में प्रति लाख SC और ST आबादी 27,973 मुद्रा ऋण SC और ST उद्यमियों को मिले, हरियाणा में 23,274 और त्रिपुरा में 21,071, जबकि भारत का आँकड़ा 12,558 है। मेघालय, नागालैंड, मणिपुर और दादरा-नगर हवेली और दमन-दीव में 1,500 से कम।
title_hi: SC और ST उद्यमियों को मुद्रा ऋण, 2022-25

title: Communal and religious riots recorded, NCRB 2024
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  RELIGION: RIOTS AS REGISTERED
subtitle:
Riot cases registered with a communal or religious motive, per crore population, NCRB 2024.
India 2.48 (349 cases). One year only.
callout_note: cases per crore people in {state}, from 3 cases in a state of 15.9 lakh people
takeaway: NCRB registered 349 communal or religious riot cases in 2024. Maharashtra had the most (90), then Bihar (80), Jharkhand (45), Odisha (37) and Karnataka (34). Per crore people, Goa is highest at 18.87 from 3 cases, then Jharkhand (11.21) and Odisha (7.93), against 2.48 for India. Sixteen states and territories registered none.
policy: The map shows one year. The older map covered 2019 to 2024 cumulatively and could not be rebuilt from the 2024 volume alone. Numbers are small, so a single case moves a small state to the top. A registration depends on police recording a riot as communal, and a zero is not proof that none occurred. Counts here are cases, and one riot can involve many victims.
takeaway_hi: NCRB ने 2024 में 349 सांप्रदायिक या धार्मिक दंगे दर्ज किए। सबसे अधिक महाराष्ट्र (90), फिर बिहार (80), झारखंड (45), ओडिशा (37) और कर्नाटक (34)। प्रति करोड़ आबादी पर गोवा 18.87 के साथ सबसे ऊपर है (3 मामले), फिर झारखंड (11.21) और ओडिशा (7.93), जबकि भारत का आँकड़ा 2.48 है। 16 राज्यों और क्षेत्रों में कोई मामला दर्ज नहीं हुआ।
title_hi: दर्ज सांप्रदायिक और धार्मिक दंगे, NCRB 2024

title: Women among MLAs, ADR 2026
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  DEMOCRACY: WHO SITS IN THE ASSEMBLY
subtitle:
Women as a share of sitting MLAs, by state assembly, as on 2 February 2026.
390 of 4,123 MLAs, 9.5%.
callout_note: of MLAs in {state} are women (19 of 90 seats)
takeaway: Women hold 21.1 per cent of seats in the Chhattisgarh assembly (19 of 90), 15.0 in Tripura and 14.8 in Jharkhand, against 1.5 in Himachal Pradesh (1 of 68), 3.3 in Jammu and Kashmir, Nagaland and Puducherry, and 4.5 in Karnataka. Across 31 assemblies 390 of 4,123 MLAs are women, 9.5 per cent. Uttar Pradesh has the most women MLAs (47) but only 11.7 per cent of its seats.
policy: Each assembly is shown on its last election as of 2 February 2026, so Assam, Kerala, Puducherry, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal are on 2021 results and have since voted. A small assembly moves a long way on one seat. Ladakh has no assembly. Women's share of Lok Sabha seats after 2024 was 14 per cent in the same report.
takeaway_hi: छत्तीसगढ़ विधानसभा में महिलाओं के पास 21.1 प्रतिशत सीटें हैं (90 में 19), त्रिपुरा में 15.0 और झारखंड में 14.8, जबकि हिमाचल प्रदेश में 1.5 (68 में 1), जम्मू और कश्मीर, नागालैंड और पुदुचेरी में 3.3 और कर्नाटक में 4.5। 31 विधानसभाओं में 4,123 में से 390 विधायक महिलाएँ हैं, यानी 9.5 प्रतिशत।
title_hi: विधायकों में महिलाएँ, ADR 2026

title: Critically polluted river stretches, CPCB 2025
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  ENVIRONMENT: RIVERS
subtitle:
River stretches in the most polluted class (BOD above 30 mg/L), CPCB report of September 2025,
from monitoring in 2022 and 2023. 36 stretches in India.
callout_note: critically polluted river stretches in {state}, level with one other state at the top
takeaway: CPCB lists 36 river stretches in its most polluted class, with biochemical oxygen demand above 30 mg/L, in 14 states and territories: Uttarakhand and Tamil Nadu have 5 each, Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat 4 and Karnataka 3. The 18 other states in the table have none in this class. Maharashtra has 54 polluted stretches in all but only 2 are critical, and Kerala has 31, none critical.
policy: This is a count of stretches, not a measure of how polluted a state's rivers are overall: states differ in river length and in how many locations are monitored. A state not in CPCB's table of 32 has no polluted stretch listed, which can mean clean water or little monitoring. The monitoring is from 2022 and 2023 and the report is dated September 2025.
takeaway_hi: CPCB ने 14 राज्यों और क्षेत्रों में अपने सबसे प्रदूषित वर्ग (जैव-रासायनिक ऑक्सीजन माँग 30 mg/L से अधिक) में 36 नदी खंड सूचीबद्ध किए हैं: उत्तराखंड और तमिलनाडु में 5-5, उत्तर प्रदेश और गुजरात में 4 और कर्नाटक में 3। तालिका के शेष 18 राज्यों में इस वर्ग में कोई नहीं। महाराष्ट्र में कुल 54 प्रदूषित खंड हैं पर केवल 2 अत्यधिक प्रदूषित।
title_hi: अत्यधिक प्रदूषित नदी खंड, CPCB 2025

title: Std V children who can read a Std II text, ASER 2024
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  EDUCATION: LEARNING
subtitle:
Share of rural government-school Std V children who can read a Std II level text, ASER 2024 (provisional).
All-India rural government schools: 44.8 per cent, up from 38.5 in 2022.
callout_note: of Std V children in government schools can read a Std II text in {state}
takeaway: In rural government schools 44.8 per cent of Std V children can read a Std II text, which means 55.2 per cent cannot. Himachal Pradesh is highest at 70.1 per cent and Jammu and Kashmir lowest at 21.8, with Nagaland 27.1, Arunachal Pradesh 27.5 and Telangana 29.3 close behind. Compared with 2022, 20 of the 27 published states improved, Sikkim by 26.4 points and Mizoram by 19.5; Tripura fell 8.0 points and Kerala 3.7.
policy: ASER tests children at home in rural districts, and these state tables cover government schools only, so they say nothing about private schools or cities. Samples are small in the smaller states, which is why Sikkim's jump should be read as a sign rather than a measurement. Reading a Std II text is a Std II skill, which is what a Std V child is expected to have.
takeaway_hi: ग्रामीण सरकारी स्कूलों में कक्षा 5 के 44.8 प्रतिशत बच्चे कक्षा 2 का पाठ पढ़ सकते हैं, यानी 55.2 प्रतिशत नहीं पढ़ सकते। हिमाचल प्रदेश में सबसे अधिक 70.1 प्रतिशत और जम्मू-कश्मीर में सबसे कम 21.8 प्रतिशत है। 2022 की तुलना में 27 में से 20 राज्यों में सुधार हुआ।
title_hi: कक्षा 5 के बच्चे जो कक्षा 2 का पाठ पढ़ सकते हैं, ASER 2024

title: Children aged 6 to 14 not in school, ASER 2024
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  EDUCATION: ENROLMENT
subtitle:
Share of rural children aged 6 to 14 not enrolled in any school, ASER 2024 (provisional).
All-India rural: 1.9 per cent.
callout_note: of rural children aged 6 to 14 are not in school in {state}
takeaway: ASER finds 1.9 per cent of rural children aged 6 to 14 not enrolled in any school. The share is highest in Meghalaya (4.1 per cent), Uttar Pradesh (3.9), Bihar (3.0), Arunachal Pradesh (2.8) and Madhya Pradesh (2.5), and Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Tamil Nadu are at 0.1. The figure is much larger for older children: 7.9 per cent of 15 and 16 year olds are not in school.
policy: These are rural household survey estimates, so they miss children in cities and migrant families surveyed elsewhere. A child counted as enrolled may still be absent: in the schools ASER visited, only 55.2 per cent of enrolled children in Bihar were present on the survey day. Small state samples mean the ranking among states near 1 per cent is not firm.
takeaway_hi: ASER के अनुसार ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में 6 से 14 वर्ष के 1.9 प्रतिशत बच्चे किसी स्कूल में नामांकित नहीं हैं। यह मेघालय (4.1), उत्तर प्रदेश (3.9), बिहार (3.0), अरुणाचल प्रदेश (2.8) और मध्य प्रदेश (2.5) में सबसे अधिक है। 15 और 16 वर्ष के 7.9 प्रतिशत बच्चे स्कूल से बाहर हैं।
title_hi: स्कूल से बाहर बच्चे, 6-14 वर्ष, ASER 2024

title: Internet subscriptions per 100 people, TRAI March 2026
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  DIGITAL ACCESS
subtitle:
Wired and wireless internet subscriptions per 100 people, end of March 2026 (TRAI).
All India: 76.6 subscriptions per 100 people, 1,092.8 million in all.
callout_note: internet subscriptions per 100 people in {state}
takeaway: TRAI counts 1,092.8 million internet subscriptions at the end of March 2026, or 76.6 per 100 people. Bihar has the fewest at 50.5 per 100, followed by Jharkhand (55.3), Madhya Pradesh (62.1) and Uttar Pradesh (62.8). Delhi (173.5), Goa (150.4), Ladakh (132.3) and Chandigarh (120.4) are highest. Rural India has 48.3 subscriptions per 100 people and urban India 126.8.
policy: A subscription is not a person. One person can hold a phone and a broadband line, or two SIMs, so figures above 100 in Delhi, Goa and Haryana say nothing about everyone being online, and the low figures in Bihar and Jharkhand do not say how many people are. Population is a projection to 2026 and the operators' rural and urban split uses different sources, so only totals are shown. Survey measures of who uses the internet (NFHS, NSS) are a separate and usually lower count.
takeaway_hi: TRAI के अनुसार मार्च 2026 के अंत में 1,092.8 मिलियन इंटरनेट कनेक्शन हैं, यानी प्रति 100 लोगों पर 76.6। बिहार में सबसे कम 50.5, फिर झारखंड (55.3), मध्य प्रदेश (62.1) और उत्तर प्रदेश (62.8)। दिल्ली (173.5) और गोवा (150.4) में सबसे अधिक। कनेक्शन व्यक्ति नहीं है, इसलिए 100 से ऊपर के आँकड़ों का अर्थ यह नहीं कि सब ऑनलाइन हैं।
title_hi: प्रति 100 लोगों पर इंटरनेट कनेक्शन, TRAI मार्च 2026

title: TB case notification rate, India TB Report 2024
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: TUBERCULOSIS
subtitle:
TB patients notified in 2023 per lakh population, public and private sector (India TB Report 2024).
25.5 lakh patients notified: 178.8 per lakh.
callout_note: TB cases notified per lakh population in {state}
takeaway: India notified 25,52,257 TB patients in 2023, a rate of 178.8 per lakh population, of which 119.7 came from the public sector and 59.2 from private providers. Chandigarh (556.4), Delhi (507.2) and Puducherry (263.5) are highest. Of the other states Haryana (260.8) and Uttar Pradesh (260.1) are highest and Kerala (61.5), Manipur (69.4) and Jammu and Kashmir (77.6) lowest, apart from Lakshadweep (9.0, on 6 cases).
policy: A notification rate counts cases found and reported, so a high rate can mean more TB or better case finding, and a low one can mean fewer cases or cases missed. The report gives no state incidence, only a national modelled figure of 199 per lakh for 2022, so this map does not show where TB is commonest. Cases are counted where they were notified, which can differ from where the patient lives, and Lakshadweep's rate rests on 6 cases.
takeaway_hi: भारत में 2023 में 25,52,257 टीबी रोगी अधिसूचित हुए, यानी प्रति लाख जनसंख्या 178.8, जिनमें 119.7 सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र से और 59.2 निजी प्रदाताओं से। चंडीगढ़ (556.4), दिल्ली (507.2) और पुडुचेरी (263.5) सबसे ऊपर हैं। बाकी राज्यों में हरियाणा (260.8) और उत्तर प्रदेश (260.1) सबसे ऊपर और केरल (61.5), मणिपुर (69.4) और जम्मू-कश्मीर (77.6) सबसे नीचे हैं।
title_hi: टीबी मामला अधिसूचना दर, इंडिया टीबी रिपोर्ट 2024

title: Share of India's inward remittances by state, RBI 2023-24
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  ECONOMY: REMITTANCES
subtitle:
Each state's share of the US$ 118.7 billion of inward remittances in 2023-24 (RBI Remittances Survey, sixth round).
Shares add to 100 per cent.
callout_note: of India's inward remittances went to {state}
takeaway: Five states received two thirds of India's inward remittances in 2023-24: Maharashtra 20.5 per cent, Kerala 19.7, Tamil Nadu 10.4, Telangana 8.1 and Karnataka 7.7, together 66.4. Bihar received 1.3 per cent and Uttar Pradesh 3.0. Maharashtra's share fell from 35.2 per cent in the 2020-21 round, while Kerala's rose from 10.2 to 19.7.
policy: A share says where remittances land in total, and it follows population as well as migration: a populous state with few emigrants can have a small share and still receive a great deal per person, and the reverse. It does not show how much a state depends on remittances, which needs state income or consumption beside it. The survey covers remittances received through formal channels for family maintenance, savings and withdrawals from non-resident deposits.
takeaway_hi: 2023-24 में भारत के आवक विप्रेषण का दो-तिहाई पाँच राज्यों को मिला: महाराष्ट्र 20.5 प्रतिशत, केरल 19.7, तमिलनाडु 10.4, तेलंगाना 8.1 और कर्नाटक 7.7, कुल 66.4। बिहार को 1.3 और उत्तर प्रदेश को 3.0 प्रतिशत मिला। 2020-21 के दौर में महाराष्ट्र का हिस्सा 35.2 प्रतिशत था।
title_hi: राज्यवार आवक विप्रेषण का हिस्सा, RBI 2023-24

title: Pupil-teacher ratio in primary schools, UDISE+ 2024-25
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  EDUCATION: TEACHERS
subtitle:
Pupils per teacher in primary schools (classes 1 to 5), all management types, UDISE+ 2024-25.
The Right to Education norm is 30 pupils per teacher.
callout_note: pupils per teacher in primary schools in {state}
takeaway: No state or territory is above the Right to Education norm of 30 pupils per teacher at primary level in 2024-25. Delhi is highest at 29, followed by Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (28), Bihar and Jharkhand (26) and Gujarat and Maharashtra (24). Ladakh (5) and Sikkim (6) are lowest. Bihar's ratio is shown as 43 in 2022-23 and 26 in 2024-25, and Delhi's as 34 and 29.
policy: A state average hides schools with one teacher for many pupils and others with too many teachers for few pupils, so a low ratio does not mean every school is adequately staffed. The figures cover government, aided and private schools together and are whole numbers. MoSPI does not say whether 2022-23 and 2024-25 are counted on the same basis, so the large fall in Bihar should be read with caution until checked against UDISE+ reports for both years.
takeaway_hi: 2024-25 में कोई भी राज्य या केंद्र शासित प्रदेश प्राथमिक स्तर पर शिक्षा का अधिकार के मानक 30 छात्र प्रति शिक्षक से ऊपर नहीं है। दिल्ली सबसे अधिक 29 पर है, फिर दादरा-नगर हवेली और दमन-दीव (28), बिहार और झारखंड (26)। लद्दाख (5) और सिक्किम (6) सबसे नीचे हैं। बिहार का अनुपात 2022-23 में 43 और 2024-25 में 26 दिखाया गया है।
title_hi: प्राथमिक विद्यालयों में छात्र-शिक्षक अनुपात, UDISE+ 2024-25

title: Rice share of cereal consumption, rural households, HCES 2023-24
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  ECONOMY: FOOD
subtitle:
Rice as a share of all cereals eaten per person per month, by weight, rural households (HCES 2023-24).
All India: 54.2 per cent.
callout_note: of cereals eaten in rural households are rice in {state}
takeaway: Rice is 54.2 per cent of the cereals eaten per person in rural India (HCES 2023-24, by weight), against 55.4 per cent in 2022-23. In 14 states and territories it is 90 per cent or more, led by Mizoram (99.6), Manipur (99.4) and Nagaland (98.4), while in Rajasthan (3.7), Haryana (7.6) and Punjab (9.3) wheat and coarse grains take most of the plate.
policy: This is a share of kilograms of cereal, not of calories or spending, and it counts household consumption from purchases, home production and free items together. A high rice share does not say how much cereal anyone eats. Rural and urban figures come from separate series, and the survey publishes no combined state figure, so the two maps should not be averaged.
takeaway_hi: HCES 2023-24 के अनुसार ग्रामीण भारत में प्रति व्यक्ति खाए जाने वाले अनाज (वज़न के हिसाब से) में चावल का हिस्सा 54.2 प्रतिशत है, जबकि 2022-23 में यह 55.4 प्रतिशत था। 14 राज्यों और क्षेत्रों में यह 90 प्रतिशत या उससे अधिक है।
title_hi: अनाज उपभोग में चावल का हिस्सा (ग्रामीण), HCES 2023-24

title: Maternal mortality ratio, SRS 2022-24
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: MATERNAL MORTALITY
subtitle:
Maternal deaths per 100,000 live births, three years pooled (SRS Special Bulletin 2022-24).
India: 87, down from 88 in 2021-23. 19 states shown separately.
callout_note: maternal deaths per 100,000 live births in {state}
takeaway: SRS puts India's maternal mortality ratio at 87 per 100,000 live births for 2022-24, one lower than 88 in 2021-23. Uttar Pradesh (154), Madhya Pradesh (135) and Chhattisgarh and Odisha (124 each) are highest. Kerala (24), Tamil Nadu (25), Maharashtra (37) and Andhra Pradesh (39) are lowest. Uttar Pradesh's 95 per cent interval (115 to 192) lies wholly above Kerala's (0 to 50).
policy: Maternal deaths are rare events, so the estimates pool three years and carry wide confidence intervals: Bihar's 96 could be anywhere from 62 to 130. Most gaps between adjacent states are within that noise, and only large gaps, such as Uttar Pradesh against the southern states, are firm. SRS shows 19 states separately and pools the rest as 'Other states' (84), so the remaining states and UTs are grey here.
takeaway_hi: SRS के अनुसार 2022-24 में भारत का मातृ मृत्यु अनुपात प्रति 1,00,000 जीवित जन्म पर 87 है, जो 2021-23 के 88 से एक कम है। उत्तर प्रदेश (154), मध्य प्रदेश (135) तथा छत्तीसगढ़ और ओडिशा (124) सबसे ऊपर हैं। केरल (24), तमिलनाडु (25), महाराष्ट्र (37) और आंध्र प्रदेश (39) सबसे नीचे हैं।
title_hi: मातृ मृत्यु अनुपात, SRS 2022-24

title: Life expectancy at birth, SRS 2019-23
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: LIFE EXPECTANCY
subtitle:
Expected years of life at birth, both sexes, SRS abridged life tables 2019-23.
India: 70.3 years. 22 larger states and UTs published.
callout_note: years of life expectancy at birth in {state}
takeaway: SRS puts life expectancy at birth at 70.3 years in India for 2019-23, up 0.4 years from 2018-22. Kerala is highest at 75.1 years, followed by Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh (74.4 each) and Delhi (74.2). Chhattisgarh is lowest at 64.6, followed by Madhya Pradesh (67.6), Uttar Pradesh (68.0) and Assam (68.6), a gap of 10.5 years between the top and bottom. Women outlive men in every state shown, by 7.1 years in Himachal Pradesh and 0.8 in Bihar.
policy: Life expectancy is a summary of the death rates of one period at every age, not a forecast of how long any child born now will live. SRS publishes it only for India and the larger states and UTs, so smaller states and the other UTs are grey, and Jammu and Kashmir includes Ladakh. The estimates come from a sample, five years pooled, so a difference of a few tenths of a year between two states is not firm.
takeaway_hi: SRS के अनुसार 2019-23 में भारत में जन्म पर जीवन प्रत्याशा 70.3 वर्ष है, जो 2018-22 से 0.4 वर्ष अधिक है। केरल में सबसे अधिक 75.1 वर्ष है, फिर जम्मू-कश्मीर और हिमाचल प्रदेश (74.4) और दिल्ली (74.2)। छत्तीसगढ़ में सबसे कम 64.6 है, फिर मध्य प्रदेश (67.6), उत्तर प्रदेश (68.0) और असम (68.6)। दिखाए गए हर राज्य में महिलाएँ पुरुषों से अधिक जीती हैं।
title_hi: जन्म पर जीवन प्रत्याशा, SRS 2019-23

title: Population with an improved drinking-water source, NFHS-6
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  HEALTH: WATER
subtitle:
Share of the household population living in households with an improved drinking-water source, NFHS-6 (2023-24).
India: 96.5 per cent, against 95.9 in NFHS-5.
callout_note: of people live in households with an improved drinking-water source in {state}
takeaway: NFHS-6 finds 96.5 per cent of India's household population living with an improved source of drinking water, against 95.9 per cent in NFHS-5. Nagaland (82.7), Jharkhand and Meghalaya (84.3 each), Lakshadweep (88.4), Madhya Pradesh (89.0) and Himachal Pradesh (89.5) are lowest, and Chandigarh, Delhi and Puducherry are highest at 99.8 to 99.9. No state reported in NFHS-6 is under 82 per cent, so the old claim of under 60 per cent in some north-eastern states does not hold on this measure.
policy: An improved source is not safe water. The survey definition counts piped water, tube wells, protected wells, rainwater, tanker trucks and bottled water, and says nothing about contamination, arsenic or fluoride, how many hours water flows, or how far it must be carried. Manipur has no NFHS-6 figure. NFHS-6 is provisional, and some state changes are large (Nagaland down 8.3 points, Himachal Pradesh down 6.7), which should be read with that in mind.
takeaway_hi: NFHS-6 के अनुसार भारत की 96.5 प्रतिशत घरेलू आबादी बेहतर पेयजल स्रोत वाले परिवारों में रहती है, जबकि NFHS-5 में यह 95.9 प्रतिशत थी। नागालैंड (82.7), झारखंड और मेघालय (84.3), लक्षद्वीप (88.4), मध्य प्रदेश (89.0) और हिमाचल प्रदेश (89.5) सबसे नीचे हैं। बेहतर स्रोत का अर्थ सुरक्षित पानी नहीं है।
title_hi: बेहतर पेयजल स्रोत वाली आबादी, NFHS-6

title: Net irrigated area as a share of net sown area, 2023-24
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  ENVIRONMENT: IRRIGATION
subtitle:
Net irrigated area over net sown area, 2023-24 provisional (RBI Handbook, from land use statistics).
India: 59.3 per cent, against 56.4 in 2022-23.
callout_note: of net sown area is irrigated in {state}
takeaway: Provisional figures for 2023-24 put 59.3 per cent of India's net sown area under irrigation, against 56.4 per cent in 2022-23. Puducherry and Punjab are at 100.0 per cent, then Haryana (91.7), Delhi (89.3), Uttar Pradesh (83.4) and Madhya Pradesh (81.5). Mizoram (6.1), Sikkim (15.7), Assam (17.0), Himachal Pradesh and Kerala (21.3 each) and Jharkhand (22.1) are lowest. The old claim that Jharkhand irrigates under 10 per cent does not hold: it is 22.1 here and 19.7 in 2022-23.
policy: The provisional year breaks the series in places, so the change since 2022-23 should be read with care: Maharashtra's net irrigated area doubles in one year (up 20 points here), and the net sown area falls sharply in Andhra Pradesh, Manipur and Jharkhand. A share of net sown area says nothing about how reliable the water is, which source it comes from or whether a second crop is irrigated. Ladakh, Chandigarh and the smaller territories are not in the source tables.
takeaway_hi: 2023-24 के अनंतिम आँकड़ों के अनुसार भारत के शुद्ध बोए गए क्षेत्र का 59.3 प्रतिशत सिंचित है, जबकि 2022-23 में यह 56.4 प्रतिशत था। पुडुचेरी और पंजाब 100.0 प्रतिशत पर हैं, फिर हरियाणा (91.7), दिल्ली (89.3), उत्तर प्रदेश (83.4) और मध्य प्रदेश (81.5)। मिजोरम (6.1), सिक्किम (15.7) और असम (17.0) सबसे नीचे हैं। झारखंड में यह 22.1 प्रतिशत है, 10 प्रतिशत से कम नहीं।
title_hi: शुद्ध बोए गए क्षेत्र में सिंचित हिस्सा, 2023-24

title: Bank offices per lakh people, March 2025
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  ECONOMY: BANKING
subtitle:
Scheduled commercial bank offices per lakh people, end-March 2025 (RBI Handbook, Table 152).
India: 11.9 offices per lakh, from 1,67,806 offices.
callout_note: bank offices per lakh people in {state}
takeaway: India had 1,67,806 scheduled commercial bank offices at the end of March 2025, 4,590 more than a year earlier, or 11.9 per lakh people. Goa has 43.4 per lakh, then Chandigarh (36.9), Ladakh (34.3), Sikkim (26.4), Lakshadweep (24.3) and Himachal Pradesh (24.2). Bihar has 6.4, Manipur 8.0, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu and Uttar Pradesh 8.1, Jharkhand 8.8 and Assam 9.0.
policy: Offices are counted where the branch stands, not where customers live, and the population is a 2024 projection against offices at March 2025. Regional rural banks, cooperative banks, post offices and business correspondents are not in the count, and in the hills and the north-east much banking reaches people through them. Small states and territories with few offices swing on a handful of branches, and a branch count says nothing about who has an account or uses it.
takeaway_hi: मार्च 2025 के अंत में भारत में अनुसूचित वाणिज्यिक बैंकों के 1,67,806 कार्यालय थे, एक वर्ष पहले से 4,590 अधिक, यानी प्रति लाख लोगों पर 11.9। गोवा में प्रति लाख 43.4 है, फिर चंडीगढ़ (36.9), लद्दाख (34.3) और सिक्किम (26.4)। बिहार में 6.4, मणिपुर में 8.0 और उत्तर प्रदेश में 8.1 है।
title_hi: प्रति लाख लोगों पर बैंक कार्यालय, मार्च 2025

title: Stage of groundwater extraction, CGWB 2024
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  ENVIRONMENT: GROUNDWATER
subtitle:
Groundwater drawn each year as a share of the annual extractable resource, CGWB 2024 assessment.
India: 60.5 per cent, against 59.3 in 2023.
callout_note: of the annual extractable groundwater is drawn in {state}
takeaway: The Central Ground Water Board's 2024 assessment has India drawing 60.5 per cent of its annual extractable groundwater, against 59.3 per cent in 2023. Five states and territories draw more than the assessment counts as recharged: Punjab (156.9 per cent), Rajasthan (149.9), Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (142.2), Haryana (136.0) and Delhi (100.8). Arunachal Pradesh (0.4), the Andamans (2.1), Mizoram (4.0), Meghalaya (4.6) and Nagaland (4.7) draw almost none.
policy: A state average hides blocks that are over-exploited inside states that look safe, and aquifers that differ in depth and recharge, so it cannot say where a well will run dry. A stage above 100 per cent is a yearly balance, not a measure of how much water is left. The figures come from the RBI Handbook's reproduction of the board's assessment, and Daman and Diu is counted with Dadra and Nagar Haveli in 2024. The earlier map counted over-exploited blocks, which is a different measure.
takeaway_hi: केंद्रीय भूजल बोर्ड के 2024 आकलन के अनुसार भारत अपने वार्षिक निकासी योग्य भूजल का 60.5 प्रतिशत निकालता है, जबकि 2023 में 59.3 प्रतिशत था। पाँच राज्य और क्षेत्र आकलन की पुनर्भरण मात्रा से अधिक निकालते हैं: पंजाब (156.9), राजस्थान (149.9), दादरा-नगर हवेली और दमन-दीव (142.2), हरियाणा (136.0) और दिल्ली (100.8)। अरुणाचल प्रदेश (0.4) में लगभग नहीं के बराबर निकासी है।
title_hi: भूजल दोहन का स्तर, CGWB 2024

title: Rice and sugarcane share of rice, sugarcane and coarse cereal area, 2024-25
eyebrow: HOW INDIA LIVES  ·  ENVIRONMENT: WATER AND CROPS
subtitle:
Rice and sugarcane as a share of the area under rice, sugarcane and coarse cereals (millets, maize, barley), 2024-25.
India: 68.8 per cent, against 68.2 in 2023-24.
callout_note: of rice, sugarcane and coarse-cereal area is under rice or sugarcane in {state}
takeaway: Rice and sugarcane take 68.8 per cent of the area under rice, sugarcane and coarse cereals in India in 2024-25, up from 68.2 per cent the year before. Punjab is at 97.3 per cent, which is 36 hectares of rice and sugarcane for every hectare of coarse cereals. Haryana is at 73.3 per cent, 2.7 to 1, so the old map's ten to one for Punjab and Haryana together does not hold for Haryana. At the other end are Rajasthan (5.3 per cent), Sikkim (16.8) and Himachal Pradesh (19.8).
policy: Rice and sugarcane are the two crops that draw most irrigation water, and coarse cereals are the dryland alternative, but this is a share of three crop groups and not a water measure. Kerala (99.8) is high because coconut, rubber and spices are outside these groups, and wheat, pulses, oilseeds and cotton are outside too. Coarse cereals include maize and barley as well as millets. Goa has no coarse-cereal area in the source and is left out.
takeaway_hi: 2024-25 में भारत में चावल, गन्ना और मोटे अनाज के कुल क्षेत्र का 68.8 प्रतिशत चावल और गन्ने के अंतर्गत है, पिछले वर्ष 68.2 प्रतिशत था। पंजाब में यह 97.3 प्रतिशत है, यानी हर हेक्टेयर मोटे अनाज पर 36 हेक्टेयर चावल और गन्ना। हरियाणा में 73.3 प्रतिशत (2.7 के मुकाबले 1) है। सबसे कम राजस्थान (5.3), सिक्किम (16.8) और हिमाचल प्रदेश (19.8) हैं।
title_hi: चावल और गन्ने का हिस्सा, 2024-25
